title: How Hackers Heated 150 Supermarket Fridges to 50C
title_notes: Sentence case; primary keyword inside the first 40 characters; no emoji; no #Shorts.
description:
How hackers heated 150 French supermarket fridges to 50C in a single night.

You'll see the one small box that runs every chilled case in a shop, why it was
answering the public internet at all, and the flaw researchers found in its login.

Attackers reached Danfoss refrigeration controllers and forced a defrost cycle that
never stopped. Intermarché said about 150 of its stores woke up warm. Claroty's
Team82 had counted 2,765 exposed AK-SM 800A controllers on the open internet when
they did their research, and CVE-2025-41450, an authentication bypass rated 8.2 out
of 10, had been fixed in firmware since 2025. Danfoss says most of the boxes that
were hit were models it no longer updates. France's CERT-FR answered with one
instruction: take the controller off the internet. Nobody has yet named who did it,
or which flaw was used.

Sources:
https://www.cert.ssi.gouv.fr/alerte/CERTFR-2026-ALE-012/
https://www.claroty.com/blog/france-supermarket-hacks-expose-risks-of-internet-facing-refrigeration-systems
https://services.nvd.nist.gov/rest/json/cves/2.0?cveId=CVE-2025-41450
https://thehackernews.com/2026/10/attackers-heat-french-supermarket.html

Animations are illustrative. Narration is a synthetic voice.

Improving AI labels for viewers and creators

synthetic_content_disclosure.rule_paraphrased: Disclosure is required for photorealistic or meaningfully altered content that appears realistic: a real person made to say something they did not say, footage of a real event or place altered, or a realistic scene that never happened. It is explicitly not required for content that is clearly unrealistic or animated, or where synthetic media is unrealistic and the changes are inconsequential.
synthetic_content_disclosure.why_no: Every frame is stylised vector animation. No real person appears, no real place or event is depicted, no footage was altered, and the voice is a stock synthetic narrator belonging to nobody. Nothing could be mistaken for a recording of something that happened.
caveats: Since 27 May 2026 YouTube can auto-apply an AI label when its systems detect photorealistic synthetic content. A detection label can be changed back to No in Studio > the video > Attributes > AI use.
Only labels from YouTube's own generative tools, or from C2PA fully-generative metadata, are permanent. This file carries no C2PA metadata.
YouTube's stated position is that a disclosure label does not affect reach or monetisation eligibility.
If you would rather disclose anyway, change the answer to Yes; nothing else in the upload changes.
